name: Squid Game
blurb: Hundreds of people in debt play deadly children's games for a giant cash prize
title: Squid Game Recap: Every Season and the Ending Explained
description: Squid Game recap: the main players, what happens in all three seasons of the Korean survival drama from 2021 to 2025, and the final ending explained.
h1: Squid Game Recap: Every Season and the Ending Explained
answer: Squid Game (오징어 게임) is a South Korean survival thriller series written and directed by Hwang Dong-hyuk. It has three seasons and 22 episodes, released in September 2021, December 2024 and June 2025; season 3 is the final season. Seong Gi-hun, a divorced, gambling-addicted chauffeur deep in debt, accepts an invitation to a secret contest on a remote island. With 455 other desperate players he competes in children's playground games for billions of won, and soon learns that losing a game means being killed.

head: Character
Who they are
rows: Seong Gi-hun (Player 456)
A kind-hearted but reckless gambler who needs money to keep seeing his daughter
Cho Sang-woo (Player 218)
Gi-hun's childhood friend, a star student turned investment manager wanted for fraud
Kang Sae-byeok (Player 067)
A guarded North Korean defector saving to bring her family to the South
Oh Il-nam (Player 001)
A gentle elderly man with a brain tumor
Abdul Ali (Player 199)
A Pakistani migrant worker whose boss has not paid him
Hwang Jun-ho
A police detective who sneaks onto the island to find his missing brother
The Front Man
The masked official who runs the games
The Recruiter
A smiling salesman who invites players by challenging them to ddakji, a Korean paper-tile game
Kang No-eul
A guard introduced in season 2, herself a North Korean defector
Kim Jun-hee (Player 222)
A pregnant young woman who enters the games in season 2

ol: Season 1 (2021, 9 episodes): In the first game, Red Light, Green Light, a giant doll watches the players and guards shoot anyone seen moving; more than half die. The survivors vote to stop and go home, but nearly all return because their lives outside are just as hopeless. Each death adds 100 million won to a prize that can reach 45.6 billion won. Gi-hun teams up with Sang-woo, Sae-byeok, Ali and the old man Il-nam. Through cutting shapes from sugar candy, tug of war, marbles and a glass bridge, the group is destroyed: Sang-woo tricks Ali out of his marbles, Il-nam is apparently eliminated after letting Gi-hun cheat, and Sang-woo kills the injured Sae-byeok. In the final squid game, Gi-hun beats Sang-woo, who stabs himself and asks Gi-hun to look after his mother. Meanwhile Jun-ho, disguised as a guard, discovers that the Front Man is his own brother, Hwang In-ho, who shoots him. A year later, Gi-hun finds Il-nam dying and learns he created the games to entertain himself and rich spectators called the VIPs. Gi-hun is about to fly to his daughter in America when he sees the Recruiter still at work; he turns back from the plane.

Season 2 (2024, 7 episodes): Three years on, Gi-hun spends his winnings hunting the Recruiter. When he finds him, the Recruiter forces him into Russian roulette and dies by his own shot. Gi-hun re-enters the games as Player 456 to end them from inside, while Jun-ho, who survived, searches the sea for the island with a boat captain. In-ho secretly joins the players as Player 001 under the name Oh Young-il and befriends Gi-hun. Players now vote after every game whether to continue, and the vote splits them into two hostile camps. Gi-hun leads a rebellion against the guards, but In-ho abandons the rebels, the uprising fails, and the Front Man shoots Gi-hun's friend Jung-bae in front of him.

Season 3 (2025, 6 episodes): A broken Gi-hun faces a deadly game of hide-and-seek, in which he kills Dae-ho, a player he blames for the rebellion's failure. Player 222, Jun-hee, gives birth during the game. When Geum-ja's son Yong-sik nearly kills Jun-hee, Geum-ja stabs him to save her, and she later takes her own life. Guard No-eul secretly helps an injured player escape. In the jump-rope game Jun-hee, too weak to cross, gives her baby to Gi-hun and jumps to her death. The VIPs let the baby take her place as a player. In-ho offers Gi-hun a knife to kill sleeping rivals, and he refuses. Jun-ho, betrayed by the boat captain who works for the games, finally reaches the island.

body: The last game, sky squid game, is played on tall platforms where players push each other off. At the end only Gi-hun, the baby and Myung-gi, the baby's father, are left. Myung-gi tries to throw the baby off and falls to his death in the struggle. To finish the game, one more player must die. Instead of sacrificing the baby, Gi-hun leaves her on the platform and throws himself off, beginning a final sentence about what humans are that he never finishes. The baby wins. In-ho carries her out as the island is evacuated. Six months later, he leaves the baby and her prize with his brother Jun-ho, then visits Gi-hun's daughter in Los Angeles to give her Gi-hun's tracksuit and winnings. Driving away, he sees an American recruiter, played by Cate Blanchett, challenging a man to ddakji: the games go on elsewhere.

ul: What Hwang Dong-hyuk has said: he first planned an ending in which Gi-hun escapes and joins his daughter in America, but changed it because it no longer fit the world he saw. He has said Gi-hun gives his life for the baby as everyone should for future generations, and that the baby stands for human conscience.
A hopeful reading: Gi-hun refuses to kill, proving the VIPs wrong about human nature, and his sacrifice even moves In-ho to save the baby.
A bleak reading: the games outlive Gi-hun, and the closing scene in Los Angeles shows that the system he fought is bigger than one island.

body.note: Hwang has said the American recruiter scene was not planned as a link to David Fincher's reported American version, and that the story does not need a sequel.

ul: Debt and inequality: every player is there because of money, and the games make the competition of a market economy literal.
The rich as spectators: the VIPs bet on the deaths of the poor, who are treated as entertainment.
Choice under pressure: the vote to continue shows that people can choose cruelty when the outside world offers them nothing.
Human decency: Ji-yeong giving up her life for Sae-byeok in the marbles game, Geum-ja and Gi-hun's final act ask whether kindness survives when it costs everything.
Childhood turned violent: the games are innocent schoolyard games, which makes the killing more disturbing.
Length: three seasons, 22 episodes of about 30 to 75 minutes. Seasons 2 and 3 form one continuous story.
Original language: Korean; dubbed and subtitled versions exist.
Content: very graphic violence, mass killings, suicide, organ harvesting and some sexual content; for adults.
The reality competition Squid Game: The Challenge is a separate show and not part of the story.

check.q: What happens to players who lose a game?
options: They are sent home with nothing
check.why: Losers are shot or die in the game itself, and each death adds 100 million won to the prize.

check.q: Who is revealed to have created the games?
check.why: At the end of season 1, the dying Il-nam tells Gi-hun he created the games.

check.q: Who wins the final game in season 3?
check.why: Gi-hun sacrifices himself so the baby is the last player left.

faq.q: Does Gi-hun die in Squid Game?
faq.a: Yes. In the season 3 finale he throws himself off the platform instead of letting the baby die, which ends the game with the baby as winner.

faq.q: Is there a Squid Game season 4?
faq.a: No. Season 3, released on June 27, 2025, is the final season, and Hwang Dong-hyuk has said the story is complete.

faq.q: Who is the Front Man in Squid Game?
faq.a: Hwang In-ho, the older brother of detective Jun-ho and a former winner of the games, who later poses as Player 001 in season 2.
